subject: Early-access pricing pathway & short pilot extension
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@olivetech.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot runway + early-commit pricing question

Hi Neha —

Quick note from our side after the demo yesterday: engineering is happy with the latency profile and embeddings look solid for search ranking. We’re approaching the end of the two-week pilot and the team wants to keep momentum. Two asks:

1) Can Redwood give us a short extension — ~3 business days — so we can run a final end-to-end test (ingest + search) with real traffic?
2) If we commit to a 6-month paid deployment by Aug 1, would you consider an "early-commit" discount or an invoice offset we could apply toward the first month?

Procurement is CC'd — they’ll want to know the mechanics (credit vs discount, invoicing timing).

We also attached a tiny usage snapshot so you can eyeball token patterns.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Product
Olive Technologies

Attachment: MVP_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 18 KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@olivetech.com>
Cc: procurement@olivetech.com
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot runway + early-commit pricing question

Alex — thanks for the note and congrats to the team on the demo. Short answers up front: yes to a brief extension; yes to an early-commit commercial option. Details below so procurement has something concrete to review.

Option A — Acceleration discount (fast-commit):
- Commit to a 6-month Dedicated plan by Aug 1.
- Redwood applies a one-time invoice credit equal to 20% of the first-month committed spend (applied to invoice month 1).
- Requires a signature on our addendum; no upfront prepayment.

Option B — Short extension + conversion credit (low-friction):
- We grant a 5-business-day pilot extension at no charge.
- If you convert to any paid plan within 30 days of the extension, Redwood issues a usage credit equal to the pilot incremental token consumption (capped at $5k).

Operational notes:
- Both options preserve the same SLA and can be formalized in a 1-page addendum.
- For procurement, we can offer an invoice workflow (standard Net30) or DocuSign for quicker signatures.

I attached a draft addendum (v1) with both paths so legal/procurement can decide which they prefer. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if that speeds things up.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: DraftAddendum_v1.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot runway + early-commit pricing question — need guidance

Marcus, Vanessa — forwarding Olive's request and the two options I proposed. Quick context: Olive is high-propensity (search product) and likely to convert if we make the conversion path low friction. Procurement is focused on invoicing mechanics rather than discount size.

My instincts: give the 5-business-day extension (Option B) to remove friction, and offer a slightly stronger early-commit credit for Option A if they sign within two weeks — 25% invoice credit instead of 20%. If we do the higher credit we should require a minimum monthly committed spend (to protect unit economics).

Questions:
- Marcus: are you comfortable with a 25% first-month credit if we add e.g., a $12k/month minimum commit?
- Vanessa: can CS accept the 5-day extension and run the extra E2E test with a small dedicated touch (one engineer for a day)?

Thanks — I’ll keep the thread going with procurement once you confirm.

-Neha

>

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot runway + early-commit pricing question — need guidance

Sounds reasonable. I can support 25% first-month credit if we get a minimum committed billing of $12,000/month for 6 months. Rationale: offsets early sales effort but preserves ARR economics.

Two minor asks:
1) Add a simple clause to the addendum that the credit is forfeited if Olive cancels within 60 days of paid start.
2) Procurement will probably ask for an itemized price table — let's include the committed monthly rate and the credit math on page 1 of the addendum.

Vanessa, happy to loop in solutions engineering if you need more runway to run the E2E test.

— Marcus

(On Fri, Jun 26, 2026 at 08:40 AM, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:)

Subject: Final proposal and addendum link — next steps

Alex / procurement team —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled this together. Per internal sign-off, here’s the final commercial path we can offer:

1) Short extension: 5 business days of pilot runtime at no charge. CS will provision one engineer for a half-day of test support (Vanessa, scheduling TBD).

2) Early-commit acceleration: If Olive signs a 6-month minimum committed plan by Aug 1 with a minimum $12,000/month, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 25% of the first-month committed invoice. Credit is applied to the first paid invoice and is forfeited if the customer cancels within 60 days of the paid start date.

Next steps:
- I uploaded a one-page addendum with the two options and the itemized price table to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABC-123-OLIVE
- Please review and sign the addendum or tell me which option you prefer and I can update the DocuSign.
- If procurement prefers Net30 invoicing instead of immediate prepay, we can invoice month 1 Net30 and apply the credit on that invoice.

If you’d like a 15-minute call to walk procurement through the addendum, I’m available Mon/Tue morning PST.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
